name: matching-1k-scenario1-load
description: What: Set the standard API key, load the 1K Scenario 1 table into the empty RetailClient entity through Connect, check every Code arrived, and back up the 'loaded' checkpoint. Why: Scenario 1 starts from this backup; Scenario 2, 3b and 3c update records by these Codes. When: once per clean install or empty baseline, before the first Scenario 1 run of this size. Needs: the model, the RetailClient matching strategy and the Connect strategy {{StrategyName}} in place; the machine's API user exists in Profisee. Success: every step Succeeded. If it fails: the failed step's description says what to fix; rerun from a restored empty baseline.

inline.description: What: Write the standard API key for the machine's API user (ConnectRuntime:ApiKeyUserName) into meta.tUser, as the Connect pack does. Why: a clean install issues its own key; every later REST and Connect call uses the standard one. Success: the user row is updated. If it fails: the user is missing from meta.tUser; add it in Profisee as a super administrator.

What: Recycle the auth, gateway and Connect pools of this instance. Why: they cache API clients, so a key written to meta.tUser is rejected (invalid_client) until they restart; only this instance's pools are touched because other instances may share IIS. Success: every named pool recycles. If it fails: a pool that does not exist fails the step; check matching/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName against IIS Manager.

steps.label: Recycle Auth, Gateway And Connect Pools

inline.description: What: Wait until every health check is Healthy. Why: services stay cold after a restore or install. Success: all checks Healthy within 10 minutes. If it fails: open the health URL and fix the service it names.

What: Call the gateway with the standard key. Why: proves the key took before Connect uses it. Success: HTTP 200. If it fails: 401 means the key did not take; recycle the instance's application pools and rerun.

What: Confirm the Connect strategy reads this size's Scenario 1 table. Why: a strategy pointed at another size loads the wrong rows silently. Success: RemoteObjectName = {{SourceTableName}}. If it fails: point the strategy at {{SourceTableName}} or create it.
What: Refuse to load into a non-empty RetailClient. Why: Scenario 1 measures matching of exactly the loaded rows. Success: 0 rows. If it fails: restore the empty baseline and rerun.

What: Start a Connect batch of {{StrategyName}}. Why: Scenario 1 data enters Profisee through Connect. Success: Connect accepts the call. If it fails: check the Connect address and the API key step above.

What: Wait for the {{StrategyName}} batch to finish. Why: the checks below need the finished load. Success: the batch reaches a successful terminal state. If it fails: read the batch errors in Connect.

What: Confirm the load kept every row and its Code. Why: Scenario 2, 3b and 3c update records by Code. Success: {{RecordCount}} rows, 0 missing Codes. If it fails: check the strategy maps Code to Code and read the batch errors.

What: Back up the Profisee database as the 'loaded' checkpoint (the start of Scenario 1). Why: every Scenario 1 run restores it. Success: backup written and verified. If it fails: check disk space in the SQL Server default backup folder.
